questions.q: What kind of compute is an Azure Virtual Machine?
options: IaaS — Microsoft manages the hardware and virtualization, you manage the OS up
SaaS — Microsoft manages the entire application for you
A managed database service with no compute component
A service that only runs pre-approved Microsoft applications
questions.explain: A VM is the same IaaS model from Lesson 2: you're responsible for the OS, patching, and everything you install on top of it.

questions.q: What kind of compute is Azure App Service, and what do you manage?
options: PaaS — you deploy your application code, and Microsoft manages the OS and runtime
IaaS — you must configure the OS and install the web server yourself
SaaS — there is no code to deploy at all
A networking-only service unrelated to running applications
questions.explain: App Service is PaaS: you bring your code in a supported language/runtime, and Microsoft handles the OS, runtime, and scaling infrastructure.

questions.q: When would a team choose a Virtual Machine over App Service?
options: When they need OS-level control or are running legacy software that requires a specific configuration
Whenever they want the fastest possible deployment with the least setup
Only when building a simple public website
Never — App Service always replaces the need for VMs
questions.explain: A VM is the right tool when full OS control is genuinely needed, such as legacy software or a specific OS dependency that App Service's managed runtime can't accommodate.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real question behind choosing between a VM and App Service?
options: Whether you need OS-level control badly enough to take on managing it yourself
Which one is more powerful in absolute terms
Which one costs exactly zero dollars
Whether the application will ever have any users
questions.explain: A VM can technically do App Service's job too — the real decision is whether the extra control is worth the extra management burden.

questions.q: What is one advantage App Service has built in that a Virtual Machine does not have by default?
options: Built-in scaling settings for handling increased traffic
The ability to run absolutely any software with no restrictions
Full control over the underlying operating system
Guaranteed zero cost regardless of usage
questions.explain: App Service includes built-in scale settings as part of the platform, whereas a VM requires you to configure scaling yourself.
